title: least-privilege iam orchestration and telemetry
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build a reusable Terraform module and companion toolchain that generates least-privilege IAM bindings and runtime RBAC policies for Private (VPC) deployments. The module should: 1) produce opinionated IAM role/policy artifacts from high-level service profiles (service identity, actions, resource scope), 2) embed validation hooks that run as part of CI to prevent overly-broad grants, 3) publish telemetry-ready metadata so Console/Optimize can surface permission changes and risk, and 4) include a small runtime health-check suite that validates role assumptions in deployed environments. Goal is to enable repeatable, auditable RBAC for on-prem/VPC installs without requiring customers to hand-edit JSON policies.
acceptance_criteria: Module accepts a YAML service-profile and emits Terraform-managed IAM roles/policy documents and IAM bindings for AWS/GCP/Azure where applicable
CI validation step rejects any generated policy with wildcard resource or '*' action unless explicitly approved via signed PR and rationale
A telemetry schema is emitted alongside each PR (policy hash, intent tags, risk score) and is ingested by Console staging for visualization
Runtime health-checks can exercise a sample token to verify role assumption and at least 5 common permission paths (read/write/list/assume) and return structured diagnostics
Documentation and examples exist for 3 customer archetypes: single-tenant VPC, shared dedicated cluster, and air-gapped on-prem
tasks: Design service-profile schema (YAML) and mapping to provider-specific IAM primitives
Prototype generator (Go) that converts YAML -> Terraform files + policy.json
Add CI job (circleci/gha) that runs OPA/Rego policies against generated JSON
Integrate telemetry export (policy metadata file) into internal telemetry pipeline
Implement runtime health-check container and small Go tool that attempts role assumptions
Write user-facing docs and migration guide for existing Terraform customers
Create demo PR and a minimal end-to-end example repo for internal reviews
decisions: Use policy-as-code (OPA/Rego) for validation rather than trying to encode complex checks inside Terraform templates — gives easier testing and reuse across CI and runtime
Keep provider-specific details pivoted behind a translation layer (generator) so service-profiles remain cloud-agnostic
Telemetry will contain hashes and intent tags but not full policy bodies in the default export to limit exfiltration risk
Generator tool will be implemented in Go to match other infra tooling and produce deterministic output for CI diffs
tradeoffs: Adding a generator introduces a new binary to maintain vs pure Terraform modules — chosen for better abstraction and validation
OPA adds complexity to CI but significantly reduces false-allow risk for policy mistakes
Emitting telemetry metadata increases visibility but requires careful redaction to avoid exposing customer-sensitive resource names
notes_and_progress: 2025-01-23: Kickoff meeting — aligned on scope and three customer archetypes; Aisha to own schema design
2025-01-30: Schema draft v0.1 posted in Confluence (link below); initial fields: service_name, actions, scopes, data_classification, intent_tags
2025-02-07: Spike complete — generator can emit Terraform AWS IAM role + policy.json for a sample service profile; proof-of-concept repo created
2025-02-21: Security review request initiated; preliminary feedback: require signed justification for any '*' action, require lineage metadata
2025-02-28: Decided to implement OPA checks in CI and provide an 'override_token' flow for approved exceptions with audit trail
2025-03-03: Prototype runtime health-check PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/priv-iam-check/pull/12 (internal), awaiting review by infra team
2025-03-05: Demo scheduled for Platform Sync on 2025-03-12; working on migration guide draft
health_checks: role-assume: attempts STS assume-role and validates returned credentials expire within expected TTL
perm-smoke-read: run sample read against core config object and verify 200 vs 403
perm-smoke-write: attempt a namespaced write to a staging resource and verify failure/success per profile
audit-log-check: ensure that actions from health-checks are emitted to configured audit sink
upgrade_strategy: Module follows semantic versioning; minor releases only add optional fields to service-profile
Provide a compatibility checker that compares existing deployed policy hashes and alerts on incompatible changes
Offer an automated migration script to map old handcrafted policy JSON into the new service-profile format where possible
rollout_plan: Week 1: internal alpha — generator + sample repo; validate with infra and security
Week 2: limited customer beta (2 customers) with dedicated support to validate migration paths
Week 3: general availability behind feature flag in private installs; telemetry collectors enabled by opt-in
Post-GA: collect feedback and iterate on Rego rules to reduce false positives
